metadata.applies_to: Both bootstrap and large-scale growth phases

findings.title: The Four Requirements
findings.summary: Every marketplace we join must pass ALL four tests. No exceptions. Failing any one disqualifies it.
findings.details:
1. API-MANAGED    Can we automate everything after sign-up?
2. GENERALIST      Can we list across many categories?
3. TRACTION        Are real buyers actually purchasing data here?
4. NO FEES         Can we list without paying to participate?

All four must pass simultaneously.

Decision rules:
  4x Pass                     → Join immediately
  3x Pass + 1x Conditional    → Join with documented exception
  Any "Investigate"            → Research before committing time
  Any "Fail"                  → Do not join

findings.title: Criterion 1: Full API-Driven Dataset Management
findings.summary: After initial sign-up, can we create, update, and manage all listings entirely through APIs — with zero manual portal interaction?
findings.details:
PASSES:
• Documented REST/GraphQL API (or CLI/SDK) for creating listings, uploading data, updating metadata, publishing revisions, managing pricing
• Full lifecycle automatable: create → push revision → update description → adjust pricing → monitor usage
• Bulk operations supported (we will have 10–20+ datasets)
• Reasonable rate limits supporting daily/weekly/monthly update cadences

FAILS:
• Listing creation or updates require a web portal
• Data uploads are manual (drag-and-drop, file picker)
• Metadata changes only possible through GUI
• Any recurring publishing step requires human interaction
• "API available" but only for read/query, not publishing

WHY: We are building an automated factory. Every manual step is a scaling bottleneck. One-time sign-up friction is acceptable. Ongoing friction is not.

findings.title: Criterion 2: Generalist Coverage
findings.summary: Can we list datasets across multiple unrelated categories without restriction?
findings.details:
PASSES:
• Supports listings across many industries (financial, geospatial, environmental, economic, demographic, etc.)
• No requirement that all listings be in a single category
• Broad category taxonomy accommodating whatever we build
• Buyer base spans multiple use cases (analytics, ML, research, BI)

FAILS:
• Platform restricts to a single domain ("financial only", "healthcare only", "advertising only")
• Technically allows multiple categories but buyer base is monolithic
• Requires data linkable to people/devices/identities (AdTech marketplaces)
• Our data would be a poor fit for the core audience across most categories

WHY: We don't know which datasets will have legs. We need marketplaces where we can cast a wide net. Niche marketplaces lock us into one bet. We want optionality.

findings.title: Criterion 3: Demonstrated Market Traction
findings.summary: Does this marketplace have real buyers making real purchases, or is it a ghost town?
findings.details:
PASSES:
• Published/verifiable metrics on provider count, listing count, buyer activity, or transaction volume
• Named enterprise customers or institutional buyers
• Active provider community with visible small/new provider success
• Operating 2+ years with evidence of growth
• Independent reviews, press coverage, or community discussion confirming real usage

FAILS:
• No verifiable buyer activity metrics
• Launched recently with no evidence of completed transactions
• Provider count inflated (registered but not active)
• Only the platform's own marketing materials reference it

ACCEPTABLE TRACTION TIERS:
  Large:  Thousands of providers, named enterprise buyers, public revenue numbers
  Mid:    Hundreds of providers, verifiable buyer community, documented transactions
  Small:  Tens of providers, but named customers and real sales evidence
  No:     No buyer evidence, only sign-ups, or "beta" with waitlist → REJECT

findings.title: Criterion 4: No Fees to Participate
findings.summary: Can we list and sell data without paying upfront fees, subscription costs, or platform access charges?
findings.details:
PASSES:
• Free to create account and list data products
• Platform monetizes through commission/revenue-share only (they earn when we earn)
• Transaction-based fees acceptable (e.g. 3% of sales, payment processing)
• Standard cloud infra costs acceptable (S3 storage, compute we'd use anyway)

FAILS:
• Monthly/annual subscription fee for provider account
• Per-listing fees
• Platform access fees separate from transaction revenue
• Required paid partnership/membership program
• "Freemium" where free tier is too limited (e.g. 1 dataset max)

NUANCE — CLOUD COSTS: AWS/Snowflake/Databricks accounts are infrastructure we need anyway. If a marketplace is embedded in a platform we already use, incremental cost to list is ~zero. But if a marketplace requires adopting a new paid platform solely to list, that is a de facto participation fee.

WHY: Revenue-share aligns incentives. Fixed fees are a tax on presence regardless of results. At startup scale, $500/month x 5 platforms = $30K/year before selling a single record.

findings.title: Scorecard: Dataset Marketplaces (all investigated)
findings.summary: All 6 dataset marketplaces pass. Databricks confirmed (was investigate). Azure added as new.
findings.details:
AWS Data Exchange
  API-Managed:  PASS   Catalog API, Data Exchange API, CLI
  Generalist:   PASS   All industries
  Traction:     PASS   3,500+ products, 300+ providers
  No Fees:      PASS   3% commission only
  VERDICT:      PASS

Snowflake Marketplace
  API-Managed:  PASS   SQL API (CREATE LISTING)
  Generalist:   PASS   All industries
  Traction:     PASS   2,700+ listings, 670+ providers
  No Fees:      PASS   0% commission
  VERDICT:      PASS

Databricks Marketplace  [CONFIRMED — was "investigate"]
  API-Managed:  PASS   REST API, Python SDK (databricks-sdk), CLI. Full CRUD.
  Generalist:   PASS   All industries
  Traction:     PASS   2,200+ listings, 230+ providers
  No Fees:      PASS   0% fee
  VERDICT:      PASS

Azure Marketplace  [NEW ADDITION]
  API-Managed:  PASS   Partner Center APIs, SaaS Fulfillment APIs v2
  Generalist:   PASS   58,000+ products, all categories
  Traction:     PASS   Massive enterprise buyer base, MACC drawdown
  No Fees:      PASS   3% flat fee
  VERDICT:      PASS

Google Analytics Hub
  API-Managed:  PASS   REST API, gcloud CLI, Terraform
  Generalist:   PASS   All industries
  Traction:     WEAK   "Underrated", lower adoption
  No Fees:      PASS   2–3% commission
  VERDICT:      PASS (weak traction)

Narrative.io
  API-Managed:  PASS   Platform APIs for ingestion + management
  Generalist:   PASS   Data-type agnostic
  Traction:     MODERATE   Buyer base skews AdTech
  No Fees:      PASS   0% from seller
  VERDICT:      PASS

findings.title: Scorecard: Other Platforms (all investigated)
findings.summary: All "investigate" items resolved. API marketplaces added. 9 platforms failed with evidence.
findings.details:
API MARKETPLACES — PASS:

RapidAPI
  API-Managed:  PASS   Full provider tooling, billing automation
  Generalist:   PASS   35,000+ APIs, 30+ categories
  Traction:     PASS   4M+ devs, Nokia-acquired, billions of calls/month
  No Fees:      PASS   20–25% commission
  VERDICT:      PASS (API delivery model, high commission)

APILayer
  API-Managed:  PASS   Providers host APIs, platform handles billing
  Generalist:   PASS   75+ curated APIs
  Traction:     PASS   Moderate, established since 2022
  No Fees:      PASS   15% commission
  VERDICT:      PASS (API delivery model)

CONDITIONAL:

Dewey Data
  API-Managed:  CONDITIONAL   No API, but white-glove managed service
  Generalist:   PASS          Multi-category
  Traction:     PASS          ~30 providers, MIT/Stanford as buyers
  No Fees:      PASS          Revenue share only
  VERDICT:      CONDITIONAL — meets spirit (zero friction), not letter (no API)

FAILED (all investigated):

Datarade      FAIL   No provider API; requires Monda ($6K+/yr) for programmatic access
Nomad Data    FAIL   No API (email-only lead-gen); thin traction (~7 employees, no Series A)
Opendatabay   FAIL   No API (uploads "being developed"); 1 FTE, 46 providers, 327 datasets
Data & Sons   FAIL   Traction unverifiable (no independent reviews or buyer metrics)
Monda         FAIL   $6K+/yr subscription fee; API only on paid Professional tier
Nasdaq DL     FAIL   Not generalist (finance-only)
Eagle Alpha   FAIL   No API (human introduction model)
Neudata       FAIL   No API (human introduction model)
Defined.ai    FAIL   Not generalist (AI training data only)

findings.title: Key Observations (Updated)
findings.summary: All investigations resolved. The bootstrap gap is real.
findings.details:
1. ALL CLOUD MARKETPLACES PASS — AWS, Snowflake, Databricks (confirmed), Google, Azure (new), Narrative.io. All have full provider APIs.

2. DATABRICKS CONFIRMED — Full REST API, Python SDK, CLI for listing lifecycle. Every step after partner approval is automatable.

3. AZURE ADDED — Passes all 4 criteria. 58,000+ products, 3% fee, full Partner Center API. Was previously excluded as "fragmented" but re-evaluated.

4. THE BOOTSTRAP GAP IS REAL — Smaller platforms universally fail on API management and/or traction. No rich ecosystem of small, easy-entry, API-managed data marketplaces exists.

5. DEWEY IS THE ONLY VIABLE BOOTSTRAP — Conditional pass. White-glove service absorbs friction. Only works because they do everything for you.

6. API MARKETPLACES ARE A NEW CHANNEL — RapidAPI (4M+ devs) and APILayer offer zero-barrier entry for data-as-API products. Different delivery model but passes all criteria.

7. NO MARKETPLACE REQUIRES EXCLUSIVITY — Multi-marketplace distribution is universally supported. List everywhere that qualifies.

8. STRATEGY SHIFT — Don't wait for bootstrap credibility. Apply to all cloud marketplaces in parallel. Use Narrative.io (self-service) and Dewey (managed) as immediate on-ramps.
